recommendation: 1. Move month-to-month customers onto longer contracts
evidence: Churn 42.7% vs 2.8% (two-year); OR two-year vs month-to-month = 0.25
suggested action: Offer loyalty discounts or added benefits for switching to 1- or 2-year plans, especially in the first year

recommendation: 2. Strengthen onboarding in the first 12 months
evidence: Churn 47.5% in the first year vs 9.5% after 4 years; OR per +1 SD tenure = 0.47
suggested action: Welcome calls, early check-ins and service-quality follow-ups for new customers

evidence: Churn 41.9% vs 19.0% (DSL); OR fiber vs DSL = 2.46 even after controlling for other factors
suggested action: Review fiber pricing, reliability and support; survey departing fiber customers

evidence: Churn 45.3% for electronic check vs 15.2% for automatic credit card; OR = 1.50 vs bank transfer
suggested action: Small incentives to switch from electronic check to automatic bank or card payment

evidence: Internet customers: churn with/without OnlineSecurity 14.6% / 41.8%; TechSupport 15.2% / 41.6%; ORs 0.68 and 0.72
suggested action: Bundle or offer free trials of online security and tech support, prioritising high-risk customers

recommendation: 6. Use the model to prioritise, not to decide alone
evidence: Contacting the top 20% riskiest customers reaches 50% of churners (top 30%: 64%)
suggested action: Score customers monthly, contact the highest-risk group first, and size the group to the retention budget

recommendation: 7. Measure impact with a controlled trial
evidence: The data are observational, so the effect of interventions is unknown
suggested action: Randomly assign retention offers within the high-risk group (A/B test) to measure their real effect before scaling
